headline: Samsung Electronics has reportedly tied up about 80% of next year's memory chip output in long-term supply contracts with big technology companies.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a specific supply figure from a Korean business outlet, but it rests on unnamed industry officials.
importance_line: It suggests big buyers such as Nvidia, Google and Microsoft are competing for scarce memory, which could keep memory dear for PC, phone and server makers and in the end for consumers, but the 80% figure comes from unnamed industry officials.
summary: KED Global reports, citing industry officials, that about 80% of Samsung Electronics' memory chip production for next year, including high-bandwidth memory (fast memory stacked beside AI processors), already has designated buyers under long-term supply agreements, with Nvidia, Google and Microsoft among the companies ordering more than five years of supply. Buyers without a contract are competing for the remaining 20% or so, and the same long-term deals are spreading to other AI parts such as capacitors, cooling equipment and power gear.
notes: KED Global page blocked here (HTTP 000). Read the English text on Bloomingbit's feed (en.bloomingbit.io/feed/news/121897), which carries the KED Global exclusive; credit kept with KED Global. Bloomingbit's own AI summary line says 'Samsung said', but the article body attributes the 80% figure to industry officials on 9 Oct; the summary follows the body.
